summary: A 1930 Glacier National Park lookout that replaced a 1927 cabin burned two weeks after completion; still standing but boarded up.

facts.design: Two-story wooden structure, enclosed 10-ft tower, 14x14-ft cab, pyramidal roof
facts.status_note: Boarded up and not used per Wikipedia

access.note: Reachable by trail; no source confirms public entry is permitted

visit.trail_note: Quarter mile below the summit of Apgar Mountain

events.note: Elevated platform and log cabin built
First structure destroyed by fire two weeks after completion (per NHLR and Wikipedia text)
Present two-story cab built; NHLR and NRHP give 1930, Wikipedia infobox and firelookout.com give 1929
Added to NRHP December 16, 1986 as part of Glacier National Park MRA

evidence.quote: An elevated platform and log cabin were built in 1927, burned two years later in a forest fire.

evidence.supports: Design and 1930 rebuild date, lowest elevation
evidence.quote: The first lookout was constructed on the site in 1929 and was destroyed by fire two weeks after completion. This identical structure was built in 1930. Located a mile high, it is the lowest elevation lookout in the Park.
The first lookout at this location was destroyed by fire in 1929, two weeks after its completion. It was immediately replaced with the present structure.
The present structure is boarded up and not used.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR/NRHP date the present structure to 1930; Wikipedia's infobox and firelookout.com give 1929. Likely the same rebuild, dated differently by source.

notes_for_editor: Build-year conflict between sources on whether the present cab is 1929 or 1930; both likely refer to the same rebuild after the 1929 fire. No staffing history found for this tower.
